messages:
sarah: heads up — after last night's KMS rekey, SCIM provisioning to Okta started failing for GSuite-backed groups. seeing 422s for group update calls and duplicate group memberships. possibly an envelope/header mismatch from the new key alias :grimacing:

alex: can you paste the failing call/response?

sarah: here are excerpts from the SCIM sync worker logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-21T01:02:12Z ERROR scim.sync Worker(34): PATCH /Groups/00ab12 failed status=422 body={"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"detail":"EncryptedExternalId header invalid","status":"422"}
2026-03-21T01:02:12Z DEBUG kms.client Encrypt: key=projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/scim-wrap v=2
2026-03-21T01:02:12Z DEBUG scim.sync payload extId=ENC(AQAB..snip..)
```

miguel: "EncryptedExternalId header invalid" sounds like the service side can't decrypt the envelope. did the rekey change the wrapper algorithm or header format?

jen: KMS rekey was a rotate that changed the key version only, not the algorithm. but we did also flip the proxy that adds the envelope metadata a week ago (header v1->v2). maybe the sync worker still expects v1.

alex: quick check — what does the verify path expect? code snippet from scim-provisioner: `if header.version != 'v2' throw InvalidExternalId`

miguel: right, and okta's SCIM connector includes that encrypted external id in the Group extension so mismatch causes the 422.

oncall-ops: I'm seeing a batch of 1.2k failed group updates starting 01:00Z, errors spike correlates with KMS rotation window. SLA alert fired.

sarah: immediate mitigation request: can we set the sync worker to accept both header versions (v1/v2) while we backfill? is that safe for security posture?

jen: quick patch would be additive parsing (try v2 then fallback to v1). security-wise it's ok short-term; we should rotate the envelope header TTL and audit the backfill usage.

alex: deploying a compatibility patch now to staging. will push to prod after smoke in ~10m.

miguel: also noticed audit logs don't show the explicit role-change events for the groups that got duplicated. KMS rotation may have pruned some audit context metadata from the envelope. need to confirm whether envelope included audit tokens.

sarah: this is the bigger concern — if audit contexts were dropped we can't tie the de-dup/regeneration to who triggered what. we need an incident path for possible RBAC drift.

oncall-ops: reopening last night's deploy logs. @idp-bot did we see any errors during envelope-proxy rollout around 23:50Z?

idp-bot: deploy-proxy-01 -> success at 2026-03-20T23:52:08Z (ci-run-id: ci-7821). No post-deploy health alerts.

jen: that matches timing — we rolled the proxy that changed header version before the KMS rotate. ordering caused clients to start emitting v2 envelopes while other parts still using v1 unwrapped keys.

alex: mitigation summary I pushed to prod: scim-provisioner now accepts v2 and falls back to v1, and safe-decryption flow logs will include key_version and envelope_version.

miguel: follow-ups: 1) backfill failed groups with a one-shot job that decrypts both v1/v2; 2) run audit reconciliation to surface any role-change gaps; 3) review deploy ordering in canary — proxy should follow KMS rotations or vice versa with a compatibility window.

sarah: agreed. I'll own 1 and 2. oncall-ops can you own 3 with infra?

oncall-ops: will do. opening an incident ticket with timeline + blast radius now. ticket: INC-2026-117.

alex: small safety note — do not re-key the KMS until backfill completes. Otherwise we risk orphaning more externalIds.

jen: also add an alert when scim.error.rate for EncryptedExternalId >= 0.5% over 5m.

sarah: thanks everyone. I'll post updates in this thread as backfill progresses. :thumbsup:
